destination.detail: Filed as a civil action under RCW 9.97.020(7), at the superior court clerk's office of the chosen qualified county, with the notice to each prosecuting attorney RCW 9.97.020(6) requires. The packet routes to the superior court of the county of conviction or adjudication because RCW 9.97.020(8) provides that it may not decline to consider the application. The superior court of the county where the applicant resides remains statutorily available and may be nearer, and a participant who prefers it may use it, but that court may decline to consider the application; if it does, it must dismiss without prejudice, must state the reason on the order, and the applicant may refile in another qualified court. There is no statutory transfer procedure: the remedy is refiling by the applicant, not transfer by the court. Confirming intake with the clerk is prudent practice and not a legal prerequisite, and it is not a condition of generating this packet; which counties require additional accompanying documents under local superior court rules is a separate open filing-instruction question.

destination.name: Civil division of the Missouri circuit court in the county of arrest
destination.detail: Filed with the clerk of the circuit court, civil division, for the county where the arrest occurred. The clerk then does three things the printed instructions on CR145 set out: issues a copy of the petition to the prosecuting attorney; sends a copy of the petition and the fingerprint card to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository at the Highway Patrol; and gives notice of the hearing to the prosecuting attorney and to each official, agency or other entity named in the petition. destination.name: The district attorney's or city attorney's office first, then the clerk of the appropriate court
destination.detail: Nevada's workflow puts the prosecutor in the middle rather than at the end: the state's own instructions direct the petitioner to prepare the petition and order, submit them to the prosecuting agency with attachments, and file with the court clerk only after the prosecutor stipulates. Local practice is material. The Clark County District Attorney will not stipulate to petitions that include municipal court arrests or convictions, so a packet covering both must go to the appropriate city attorney and then to the district attorney, with a separate signature line for each prosecuting agency on the order. Only one petition, affidavit and order is required to seal all records within Clark County, and justice court petitions must be captioned to the specific township. Las Vegas Municipal Court requires its own Petition, Declaration and Verification, Order and Stipulation and denies typed signatures outright. Reno Municipal Court charges a filing fee, sets the petition for hearing at least 60 days after filing, and applies the sex trafficking fee exemption.

routes.publicLabel: The automatic vacatur, dismissal and expungement, and how to check it
routes.statuteOrAuthority: Marihuana Regulation and Taxation Act; N.Y. Crim. Proc. Law § 160.50; N.Y. Crim. Proc. Law § 160.50(3)(k); N.Y. Crim. Proc. Law § 160.50(5)(a); N.Y. Crim. Proc. Law § 160.50(5)(b)(i); N.Y. Crim. Proc. Law § 160.50(5)(b)(ii); N.Y. Crim. Proc. Law § 160.59
routes.participantFacingInstrument: no filing — process guidance: The automatic vacatur, dismissal and expungement, and how to check it

destination.name: The New York court in which the person was convicted
destination.detail: Two stages with two different answers. The vacatur, dismissal and expungement happen by operation of law under CPL § 160.50(5)(a): nothing is filed, nothing is generated and the participant does nothing, while under § 160.50(5)(b)(i) the chief administrator of the courts notifies the Division of Criminal Justice Services and the police, district attorney and other law enforcement agencies that hold the records. The destruction request is a participant submission to a court. The form directs "Submit your application to the Court where you were convicted", and the instructions page adds that an application sent to a different court cannot be processed and that a person with eligible convictions in more than one court must submit a separate application to each. The Office of Court Administration publishes the form; it does not receive it, and there is no statewide OCA address, mailbox or portal for this application. What happens after submission belongs to the court: it returns an Acknowledgement of Application to Destroy Expunged Marihuana Conviction Record and forwards the application to the prosecutor, the law enforcement agencies involved and, where the person was fingerprinted, DCJS, which then writes to confirm destruction. Those are the court's acts and none of them is the participant's to perform.
